newsitem.title: USA: Romania presses NATO case in Washington.
newsitem.headline: Romania presses NATO case in Washington.

text.p: U.S. and Romanian defence leaders on Tuesday discussed Romania's push to gain early entry into NATO, but Washington said again it had not yet taken a position on candidates for alliance enlargement.

U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen said at a photo opportunity with visiting Romanian Defence Minister Victor Babiuc that Bucharest had support from a number of countries, but he stressed that Washington had made no decision.
"Obviously, this is something that only NATO can pass judgment on at its (summit) meeting in July" in Spain, Cohen told reporters.

"The United States has taken no position with respect to any of the countries who have been at least considered for recommendation for accession into NATO. That has to await the judgment of the full NATO members."
Of the 12 former eastern bloc countries to apply, Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are widely considered the front-runners to be invited to apply for early membership in the Atlantic alliance.

Babiuc's visit follows a recent Washington trip by Romania Foreign Minister Adrian Severin to press his country's move to gain entry to NATO among the first wave of former Soviet allies in Eastern Europe to join NATO.
A State Department spokesman said last week that Washington would not decide until May or June, ahead of the Madrid summit in July, on whom to support.
Diplomats in Brussels said this week that France, supported by southern European NATO members, was backing Romania's application in the face of coolness from the United States, Britain and Germany.

A reformist government took over from former Communists in Romania last year, and Cohen on Tuesday praised "tremendous strides" in democratic advancement which the country has made since the Warsaw Pact broke up.
Babiuc told reporters he wanted to discuss bilateral military relations with Washington, NATO enlargement and U.S. military help in helping his country adapt to alliance military standards.

"I will try to convince the U.S. officials that (NATO) expansion has to be done on both flanks, North and South, because otherwise the coherence of the alliance will be affected," he said without elaboration.
In Brussels on Monday, Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea accompanied by Severin continued his country's concerted efforts to woo support from NATO members for early entry.
Ciorbea and a sizeable delegation met a series of ambassadors to the North Atlantic Treay Organisation to argue Romania's case for joining the first wave of entrants.
Ciorbea said the 16-nation alliance promised Romania a democratic bulwark for his country's newly elected government.
